If I could change one thing about iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would disable the new downward swipe gesture to summon Siri AI. There are already plenty of ways to invoke Siri, and I've always been used to swiping down on my iPhone and iPad to open Notification Center, so this new action doesn't affect my habits either.

As for the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even as late as the end of August, new beta versions are still adding welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes it harder to see the battery percentage on MacBook

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery control item in the menu bar. By default, it doesn't show the percentage—just a battery-shaped icon.

At first glance, this state doesn't seem problematic. I've even disabled the percentage display on my own iPhone, which uses a similar battery icon. However, I've always liked seeing the percentage on my Mac.

If you enable the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, that number will be placed inside the battery icon. I assume Apple is trying to maintain consistency with the iPhone design in iOS 27.

Placing the percentage inside the battery icon on the iPhone was a compromise Apple made to address the cramped area to the right of the notch or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, I'm not dealing with a lack of screen space.

I've been using macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air since the first developer beta. I found that I overall check the battery percentage less often because it's harder for my eyes to see.

I hope Apple will reconsider this in future design decisions, especially if more users find it problematic. In the meantime, I've at least solved the problem myself.

I used Codex to create a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays the battery status and percentage I want. If you find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
